title: G-TEK Cyborg 87-Key Cherry MX Red Mechanical Tenkeyless Keyboard $69 (RRP $249) Shipped @ LaserCo
body:

[CrispyChrispy] Laser's GTEK stuff is literally just rebranded OEM stuff straight from AliEx with a price jacked up 200%. This keyboard is non-hotswap too.
Built for Gamers. Designed for Performance.
Yeah not in 2026 buddy, hall effect switches are the bare minimum
[Kemikemi] Good comments but where are your links to the Aliexpress keyboards equivalent to the one I posted?
[CrispyChrispy] I can't post AliEx links in comments here unfortunately, but if you're mainly interested in gaming performance there's quite a few Aula, Womier, Attack Shark and Epomaker 65% hall effect boards around this price or cheaper. Amazon has a few decently priced options too, though AliEx would likely work out quite a bit cheaper when cashback and coupon deals roll around. TBH hall effect TKL boards are not super common, though they are out there.
If you're not after a hall effect board there are many decent TKL and 75% boards that will offer better features such as gasket-mount (better typing feel and sound), bigger batteries (many of them 4000mAh), pre-lubed switches and stabs, hotswap capability, screens, knobs, etc. They're not all good, some may require dodgy software to configure, but will still offer a lot more overall than this GTEK board.
IMO best bang for buck boards sit at around the ~$100 AUD mark, your options open up quite a bit more at that price range.

[CrispyChrispy] Cherry switches were all the rage ~10 years ago, but they've largely been superseded by Chinese switch manufacturers in quality, variety and value. You won't find many newer boards using them anymore (unless they're from Logitech, Corsair, Hyper X, etc. but IMO many of those brands are overpriced and stuck in the past - they're slowly getting better though)
